results.summary_before: This 8-bit serial-in ALU processes two operands shifted in LSB-first and supports eight operations including ADD, SUB, AND, OR, XOR, and NOT. It provides a parallel result and status flags (carry, zero, negative, overflow, done) after 16 clock cycles. Testing involves shifting in operands and reading the result and flags, and it can be interfaced with a microcontroller or manual switches. The design is notable for its serial interface, which reduces pin count while maintaining full ALU functionality.

results.summary_before: This is an 8-bit CPU that loads 16-bit instructions over SPI into internal program memory and then executes them autonomously. A RUN input starts execution, while PROGRAM_LOADED, HALTED and RUN_ECHO pins report status, and the eight outputs expose the CPU result byte. The final stable version uses ten instruction slots and an enriched ISA, though the documentation does not list the instruction set. No external hardware beyond an SPI host is described.

results.summary_before: This project implements a 4-neuron spiking neural network using the Leaky Integrate-and-Fire model. Each neuron integrates input current, leaks a fraction of its membrane potential, and fires a spike when the threshold is reached. The weight matrix is programmed serially via a shift register, and spike outputs are provided for each neuron. The design is tested by programming weights and observing spike outputs; no external hardware is required.

results.summary_before: This is a simple stopwatch that counts in hundredths of a second and displays the time on an 8-digit 7-segment display via SPI using a MAX7219 chip. It includes start/stop, lap time, and reset inputs, with outputs for SPI MOSI, CS, and CLK, as well as status signals. The design divides a 1 MHz clock to 100 Hz to drive the counters. External hardware needed includes buttons for control and a MAX7219-compatible display.
